patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and LeadIQ share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and LeadIQ share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Hunter only if your buying job matches “Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; St” rather than LeadIQ's shape. Choose LeadIQ only if your buying job matches “Chrome/LinkedIn-adjacent capture and CRM sync with Universal Credits — Free 50 credits; Pr” rather than Hunter's shape. Workflow advantage: Hunter leans email-outreach; LeadIQ leans lead-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and LeadIQ share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hunter is Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; Starter from $49/mo.; LeadIQ is Chrome/LinkedIn-adjacent capture and CRM sync with Universal Credits — Free 50 credits; Pro from $200/mo..
- Company-size focus: Hunter (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs LeadIQ (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Hunter-leaning email-outreach vs LeadIQ-leaning lead-management.
- Researched limits: Hunter — Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; LeadIQ — Pro starts at $200/mo — higher entry than many SMB contact tools.

Limitations — Hunter: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Lead scoring is limited versus enterprise SI platforms; LeadIQ: Pro starts at $200/mo — higher entry than many SMB contact tools; Native email sequencing depth is limited versus dedicated engagement platforms.

Poor-fit cases: Hunter is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database · LeadIQ is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pro starts at $200/mo — higher entry than many SMB contact tools · Avoid Hunter if you actually need LeadIQ's motion (Chrome/LinkedIn-adjacent capture and CRM sync with Universal Credits — Free 50 c)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
